source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / céginformációs szolgáltatók – GIRO Zrt. cégadatok és pénzügyi mutatók
why_relevant: Company-register-derived financial data on the operator (revenue, equity, ownership by the MNB/banks) — a cross-check on the operator's own annual accounts and a proxy for clearing-fee revenue trends. Statutory filings are also obtainable from e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Fogalomtár és szakmai anyagok
why_relevant: Banking association glossary that authoritatively fixes Hungarian clearing/settlement terminology (elszámolás, kiegyenlítés, klíring, KELER, BKR), which is the basis for reliable local-language query construction and entity disambiguation across this cell.

source_name: Wikipédia (hu) – Azonnali Fizetési Rendszer és GIRO rendszer szócikkek
why_relevant: Cheap entity/alias map and citation trail for AFR, GIRO, BKR, InterGIRO1/2, GIROInstant — useful for snowballing to primary sources and for resolving naming variants, but never citable as evidence itself.

source_name: NAV – Tájékoztatás az Azonnali Fizetési Rendszerről (public-sector participant view)
why_relevant: Tax authority guidance on how AFR/secondary account identifiers apply to state collections — evidence of public-sector adoption of the instant scheme, a material volume driver for the operator.

source_name: Akadémiai szakirodalom – A magyarországi bankközi klíringrendszer működése (PhD disszertáció, ME GTK)
why_relevant: Doctoral research on the operation of the Hungarian interbank clearing system; compiles long historical BKR series and methodology notes that help interpret definitional breaks in operator statistics.

source_name: eGov Hírlevél – GIRO Bankközi Klíring Rendszer (BKR) tárgycímke archívum
why_relevant: Long-running Hungarian e-government newsletter with a dedicated BKR tag — a curated chronological archive of BKR/AFR developments useful for reconstructing the timeline and finding older operator announcements no longer on giro.hu.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) - main site
why_relevant: Peak association of Hungarian credit institutions (founded 1989). Publishes sector position papers, communiques, press releases and periodic banking-sector commentary; the central node for HU banking industry intelligence and the natural entry point to member lists, journals and reports.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség - Tagjaink (member institutions list)
why_relevant: Fetched page lists roughly 67 full and associate member institutions - OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste, CIB, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, foreign branches (Deutsche Bank, BNP Paribas, ING, Citibank Europe), mortgage banks, savings institutions, plus payment/market infrastructure members KELER and BISZ. This is the master actor map for the whole HU institutional landscape.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség - Publikációk (publications hub)
why_relevant: Hub for association studies, reports and journals; the practical route to recurring sector analyses rather than one-off press items.

source_name: Gazdaság és Pénzügy (G.É.P.) - Banking Association quarterly journal
why_relevant: Peer-style quarterly published by the Banking Association (with the Foundation for Financial Culture Development), ISSN 2677-1314 online. Carries articles on payments, digitalisation, cash usage and banking-sector economics - a durable analytic corpus. Also archived openly in REAL-J (MTAK).

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség - Sajtóközlemények / Kommunikék (press releases & communiques)
why_relevant: Fastest signal channel for the banking industry's stance on payment regulation, interchange, cash-acceptance mandates, transaction levies and digital payment initiatives; often the first public sector-aggregate figures.

source_name: Bankszövetségi Krónikák (Kovács Levente) - association chronicle PDF
why_relevant: Book-length compilation including 2024 member institutions and extracts from the Association's annual-report management summaries - a rare consolidated historical baseline for the HU banking sector and its digital transition.

source_name: Országos Kereskedelmi Szövetség (OKSZ) - Hungarian Trade Association
why_relevant: Principal retail-sector interest body (founded 1990); members include Hungary's six largest food retail chains plus IKEA, Metro, Media Markt, Praktiker, dm, Foodora; member turnover reportedly exceeds HUF 5,000bn and ~1/3 of retail sales. Directly and repeatedly on the record about card acceptance vs. mandatory cash acceptance - the merchant/acceptance side of card and cash usage.

source_name: EFISZ - Elektronikus Fizetési Szolgáltatók Szövetsége (Electronic Payment Service Providers Association)
why_relevant: The single most payment-specific association in the cell. Founded by nine payment-infrastructure heavyweights (GIRO Zrt., Magyar Posta, Magyar Telekom, OTP, MKB/Budapest Bank, Pénzjegynyomda, the savings-cooperative integration body, Nemzeti Mobilfizetési Zrt.). Runs its own consumer research on electronic payment awareness and use - primary payment-behaviour data outside the central bank.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA)
why_relevant: Umbrella body for the domestic fintech ecosystem across membership tiers (startup, scale-up, ecosystem organiser, supporting member), spanning payment solutions, aggregators, AML, crypto and banks. Its member roster is a pointer to the non-bank payment-provider landscape (e.g. Barion, SimplePay); its position papers address fintech's GDP contribution.

source_name: MKIK - Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara (Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry)
why_relevant: Statutory national chamber; runs recurring enterprise surveys (minimum wage research, FX rapid surveys) that break out the 'financial and insurance services' sector, plus TOP100 corporate research with Corvinus and Pécs. Gives demand-side and SME-side context for payments and banking.

source_name: MKIK GVI - Gazdaság- és Vállalkozáskutató Intézet (Institute for Economic and Enterprise Research)
why_relevant: The chamber's research arm; has run semi-annual business-cycle surveys of Hungarian firms since 1998 with GDP-forecasting output, and publishes downloadable study PDFs. Best-structured, longest time-series association-side survey data in the cell.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség (Hungarian Leasing Association) - quarterly market statistics
why_relevant: Publishes quarterly and annual leasing-market volumes with segmentation (e.g. HUF 909.46bn placements, 72,330 contracts, split SME 66% / large corporate 16% / individuals 6.3%). Association-aggregated member data of exactly the kind A4 needs for non-bank credit adjacent to payments.

source_name: Magyar Faktoring Szövetség (Hungarian Factoring Association) - Statisztikák
why_relevant: Maintains a dedicated statistics page with member-aggregated factoring turnover and GDP penetration (turnover reported rising HUF 6,513bn to 8,023bn; penetration 7.9% to 9.2% vs ~12.5% EU average). Clean, recurring association statistics series.

source_name: IVSZ - Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége (Association of Digital Enterprises, formerly IT/telecom association)
why_relevant: Leading interest body for the digital economy; its digitalisation positions and member base overlap with payment-technology vendors, POS/terminal integrators and IT suppliers to banks. Useful for the technology-supply side of the payments value chain rather than for payment statistics themselves.

source_name: MNKSZ - Magyar Nemzeti Kereskedelmi Szövetség (Hungarian National Trade Association)
why_relevant: Second retail-side association alongside OKSZ, weighted toward domestically owned chains; publishes member and partner directories and participates in legislative consultation. Complements OKSZ for the acceptance side and for domestic-vs-international merchant split.

source_name: Magyar Franchise Szövetség (Hungarian Franchise Association)
why_relevant: Founded 1991 as the interest body of the franchise business community; its member list maps multi-site retail and hospitality networks that are POS/acceptance customers - a useful secondary merchant-side actor map.

source_name: HVCA - Magyar Kockázati- és Magántőke Egyesület (Hungarian Private Equity and Venture Capital Association)
why_relevant: Founded 1991, ~70 members, full member of the European VC/PE association; publishes quarterly investment statistics (e.g. HUF 31.079bn into 38 companies across 39 deals in a quarter). Tracks capital flowing into Hungarian fintech/payment startups - the funding lens on the payments ecosystem.

source_name: MABISZ - Magyar Biztosítók Szövetsége (Association of Hungarian Insurance Companies) and its Szemle
why_relevant: Insurance peak association; its Szemle press-review republishes financial-sector items (e.g. factoring-market coverage) and MABISZ itself publishes member-aggregated insurance market statistics. Adjacent financial-sector benchmark and a secondary aggregator of HU financial trade news.

source_name: BKIK - Budapesti Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara (Budapest Chamber of Commerce and Industry)
why_relevant: Territorial chamber that republishes and localises MKIK rapid surveys, including one on the forint-euro exchange rate showing notably strong negative effects among financial and insurance services firms - i.e. sector-broken-out survey data usable for A4 context.

source_name: Pest Vármegyei és Érdi Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara - Felmérések, kutatások
why_relevant: Example of the county-chamber layer (there are ~19 territorial chambers, e.g. Zala: zvkik.hu) each hosting survey and research pages; regional granularity for SME payment behaviour and business conditions that the national chamber aggregates away.

source_name: FinTechZone / Fintech.hu - association-tracking trade media (EFISZ, HFA tag feeds)
why_relevant: Trade media that systematically covers Hungarian payment/fintech associations and often carries association research summaries earlier and more accessibly than the associations' own sites; tag pages act as ready-made monitoring feeds and pointers to new association formations.
